Isn't it... somewhat of a bad idea to have docs#WithTop.instSupSet as an instance?

To explain my situation: I have some type α which has all non-empty infima, but does not have most suprema. I proved that WithTop α is a complete lattice, and my idea was to then define the supremum on α as WithTop.untopD default (sSup ((↑) '' s)), i.e. the supremum on the complete lattice, or a default value if it lands at ⊤. Except, I can't actually do this, because there are now two different instances of SupSet (WithTop α), the first coming from the complete lattice instance, the second coming from SupSet α → SupSet (WithTop α). And of course, the latter has terrible def-eqs.

Is this instance problematic? Or am I doing something wrong?
This instance is problematic in that we need to obliterate this as a class entirely.
As in you believe docs#SupSet should be Prop-valued instead? I could certainly agree. This is what happened to general limits in category theory land
I mean I think it should be notation for the Classical.choose of an LUB if one exists, or else the default value.
Can you think of a single instance where there are interesting defeqs on docs#sSup ? (okay, I can think of one... can you think of two?)
I suppose I'm asking what the principle should be here
The principle is that if there aren't ever going to be good defeqs, then making everything go through Classical.choose is reasonable

no I mean I agree
but I'd personally want a lot more data obliterated
I think the problem is that this creates diamonds?
No, obliterating data helps to remove diamonds. That's why we prefer Prop-valued classes. The negative consequence is that there are less defeqs, so you need to do more explicit rewrites in proofs.
hmm, I am no longer convinced this is a bad idea

Oh I see
Yeah we're never calculating explicitly with sSup. Get rid of it I agree.
